Rajendra Chola was a powerful South Indian emperor who expanded the Chola empire significantly.
Rajendra inherited a strong foundation from his father, Rajaraja I, and became co-regent in 1012 CE.
Rajendra Chola launched successful military campaigns, including a famous northern expedition to the Ganges, earning him the title 'Gangaikond'.
He built the majestic Gangaikondacholapuram Temple, home to South India's largest Shivling, and shifted the capital there.
